title: Operational KPI Glossary + Mini Tracker
summary: Compact working glossary of key operational metrics for quarterly customer reviews, plus a lightweight tracker table customers can copy into QBR decks. Purpose: make fast, consistent conversation points across CS, solutions, and eng when reviewing latency, uptime, cost/token, and cache hit tradeoffs.
body:
Context:
This is a bite-sized working doc intended for CS owners prepping a 30–45 minute QBR with engineering partners and the customer. Not a canonical spec — use as a checklist + table to export into slide(s).

How to use this file:
- Copy the glossary rows into your QBR slide, fill values from the product dashboard (per-route/model) and annotate actions.
- If a metric is off-SLO, include a root-cause note and next-step owner.

Metric definitions (practical, operational):
1) 95th percentile request latency (ms):
- What we measure: end-to-end server-side token response latency at the 95th percentile for completed generation requests. This excludes client-side network time and streaming downstream latency. Use 95p to highlight tail behavior customers feel.
- Why it matters: tail latency impacts user experience more than median; alerts should target 95p breaches.
- Measurement notes: 95p over rolling 7d and 30d windows; split by route/model and by region.
- Quick diagnostic signals: high KV cache miss rate, large prompt length, model fallback to larger variant, batch size spikes.

2) Uptime / Availability (%):
- What we measure: percent of requests successfully returned (200 or 206 chunked) divided by total incoming requests in the window. Excludes planned maintenance per SLA.
- Why it matters: availability is top-level renewal signal; even infrequent failures degrade trust.
- Measurement notes: report both request-level availability and node-level health checks. Provide incident summaries for any <99.9% windows.
- Quick diagnostic signals: region-level capacity exhaustion, autoscaler misconfig, transient RPC errors to GPU backends.

3) Cost per token (USD/token):
- What we measure: realized infra cost allocated to customer requests divided by total tokens generated in the period (includes compute, queued-billing adjustments, and model-specific amortized licensing when applicable).
- Why it matters: customers care about unit economics as usage scales. Gives a baseline for cost-optimization discussions (batching, quantization, smaller model families).
- Measurement notes: provide both raw and normalized (same prompt mix) cost/token for month-over-month comparison. Flag large jumps with root cause (pricing change, model swap, bad prompts).
- Quick diagnostic signals: sudden increase in average generation length, fallback to non-quantized variant, increased retry rate causing duplicated work.

4) KV / prefix cache hit rate (%):
- What we measure: percentage of generation requests that hit the prefix (KV) cache such that token decode time is materially reduced versus cold-start. Measured per route/model and weighted by request volume.
- Why it matters: cache hits reduce latency and tokens billed on the heavy model; improving hit rate is an efficient lever for cost/latency.
- Measurement notes: report both raw hit rate and effective hit-rate-wt (weight by tokens saved). Show typical prefixes that miss (e.g., long dynamic user context).
- Quick diagnostic signals: authoring changes to prompt template, increased per-request context variability, cache key mismatches after deploy.

Mini tracker table (copyable into slides) — replace bracketed values:
- Customer: [Name]
- Review period: [YYYY-MM-DD to YYYY-MM-DD]
- Owner (CS): [name]  Eng contact: [name]

Metric | Current window | Target SLO / Threshold | Delta vs prior period | Notes / action owner
95p latency (ms) | [e.g. 420] | [<= 300] | [+120] | [Large prompt mix; engage solutions-engineering — Jonah] 
Availability (%) | [99.992] | [>= 99.95] | [-0.003] | [Node flapping in eu-west1; SRE investigating — Lena]
Cost / token (USD) | [0.00095] | [<= 0.0009] | [+6%] | [Shift to hd-quantized variant scheduled — Marco]
KV cache hit rate (%) | [58] | [>= 70] | [-12] | [Prompt templates changed; CS to review with customer — Aisha]

Suggested remediation playbook (short bullets):
- Latency: sample slow requests, capture full prompt lengths and cache keys, validate model variant mapping. Consider temporary routing to lower-sequence variant for interactive flows.
- Availability: escalate with SRE, collect node-level logs and recent deploys, tag incidents in the tracker, and schedule postmortem for >1h disruptions.
- Cost/token: run a prompt-mix normalized cost analysis, propose batching or quantization, and simulate cost delta for proposed model swap before committing.
- Cache hit rate: compare pre/post deploy cache key generation, add deterministic prefixing where safe, and increase cache TTL for stable prefixes.

Conversation prompts for QBR (quick starters):
- "We saw a 40% jump in 95p latency for route X; are these interactive flows or background jobs?"
- "Availability dipped under our 99.95% target for 6 hours — do you want a full postmortem or a tactical mitigation?"
- "Given the current cost/token trajectory, would you accept a small quality delta if it cuts cost/token by 15%?"
- "Are recent prompt template changes expected? If not, we should lock templates to improve cacheability."

Appendix: quick data pulls to run before the QBR (commands / dashboards):
- Per-route 95p latency, 7d and 30d windows (Console > Models > Route > Metrics).
- Request-level samples for top 5 slowest requests in the period (export logs).
- Cost/token breakdown by model and quantization tier (billing export + cost-allocation mapping).
- Top 50 prefixes by volume and their cache hit/miss rates (cache dashboard).

Notes to self / TODOs:
- Convert this into a one-slide checklist and a separate CSV tracker.
- Add example alert thresholds we iterate on with SRE.
- Validate cost/token accounting with finance for external-facing QBRs.

End of doc.
